criteria.title: Functional scope and the immutability decision

levels.0: Lists create and redirect only, or wanders into link-in-bio pages, QR codes and billing without being asked.
levels.1: Covers create, redirect, custom aliases, expiry and analytics, but never decides whether destinations can be edited.
levels.2: Covers create (alias, expiry), redirect, disable/delete and minutes-fresh analytics, and explicitly makes destinations immutable because it makes every cache correct by construction.

criteria.title: Non-functional targets, including correctness and unguessability

levels.0: No latency or availability targets; correctness of the mapping is never mentioned.
levels.1: States latency and availability, but treats 'never the wrong URL' and 'hard to enumerate' as afterthoughts.
levels.2: Under 50 ms p99 added, redirect availability higher than create availability (e.g. 99.99% vs 99.9%), no code ever resolves elsewhere, codes not enumerable, and analytics that must never affect redirects.

levels.0: No numbers, or numbers stated without derivation.
levels.1: Gets roughly 40 writes/s and 4,000 reads/s but no peak, or a peak with no stated assumption.
levels.2: 100M ÷ 2.59M s = 38.6 writes/s; ×100 = 3,860 reads/s; ~3,900 total; 5× peak ≈ 19,500/s; and concludes the write path is trivial so the design effort belongs on reads.

criteria.title: ID space, storage and cache sizing

levels.0: Picks a code length without arithmetic.
levels.1: Computes 6B links and some storage figure, but not the fraction of the ID space used or why 6 characters is not enough.
levels.2: 62⁷ = 3.52T vs 6B links (0.17% used), shows why 6 chars fails unguessability (about 1 in 10 guesses hits), ~3 TB (9 TB replicated), and a day's working set of ~15 GB that fits in cache.

levels.0: Endpoints named without request or response shapes or status codes.
levels.1: POST and GET with bodies, but no idempotency, no 409 for taken aliases, or no distinction between 404 and 410.
levels.2: POST /v1/links with Idempotency-Key, 201 body, 409 / 400 / 429; GET /{code} returning 302 with Location and Cache-Control; 404 vs 410; cursor-paged list and a stats endpoint.

levels.0: Says 'a database' or picks one with no reasoning.
levels.1: Keys links by code and picks SQL or NoSQL with a generic reason ('NoSQL scales').
levels.2: Partition key = code, a separate owner index, conditional insert-if-absent for uniqueness, write ordering so a crash leaves a harmless state, and a choice decided by access pattern and operations (with sharded Postgres named as a valid alternative).

levels.0: A box diagram with no walkthrough.
levels.1: Walks the redirect through LB, service, cache and store, but the create or analytics path is missing.
levels.2: Walks redirect (in-process cache → Redis → store, expiry check, async click event, latency budget), create (idempotency, validation, insert-if-absent, negative-cache delete) and analytics separately, over a multi-AZ layout.

levels.0: Uses an auto-increment counter or a truncated hash with no collision handling.
levels.1: Compares a couple of options but misses enumeration or the birthday-collision math.
levels.2: Compares hash, counter (+ ticket server or ranges), Snowflake (11 chars) and random; quantifies collisions; chooses by write rate and unguessability (e.g. random + conditional insert), and says when to switch to counter + keyed permutation.

levels.0: Picks 301 or 302 without knowing the difference.
levels.1: Knows 301 is cached by browsers and picks 302, but has no staleness bound per layer or no hot-key plan.
levels.2: Explains 301's default cacheability and what it does to analytics, expiry and deletion; picks 302 with a max-age; gives each layer a TTL/invalidation; covers negative caching with invalidation on create, hot keys and request coalescing.

criteria.title: Analytics off the hot path; aliases and expiry

levels.0: Increments a counter in the database on every redirect, or reuses expired codes.
levels.1: Sends click events asynchronously, but no plan for broker outage or duplicates; expiry relies on store TTL.
levels.2: Buffered async events that fail open with a dropped-events metric, idempotent aggregation, HLL for uniques; expiry checked on read, codes never reused (tombstones), aliases through the same conditional insert.

levels.1: Covers instance and zone loss, but not a cold cache, broker outage, or what breaks first at 10×.
levels.2: Sizes the store for a cold cache, covers zone loss with headroom (N+1), broker outage, enumeration scans; at 10× names the cache/hot keys first, the move to 8-char codes, and the multi-region code-collision problem with last-writer-wins.

levels.1: Names trade-offs generically (consistency vs availability) without tying them to this design.
levels.2: Each key decision (ID scheme, code length, 302, immutability, KV store, async analytics, no reuse) comes with the alternative and the specific reason it lost here.
